{{Short description|Disk encryption system for FreeBSD}}
'''geli''' is a [[block device]]-layer [[disk encryption]] system written for [[FreeBSD]], introduced in version 6.0. It uses the [[GEOM]] disk framework. It was designed and implemented by Paweł Jakub Dawidek.<ref>{{cite web
| url=https://www.freebsd.org/doc/en_US.ISO8859-1/books/handbook/disks-encrypting.html
| title=Encrypting disk partitions
| author=Lucky Green
| work=FreeBSD handbook
| access-date=2015-06-14}}</ref>

== Design details ==
geli was initially written to protect data on a user's computer in situations of physical theft of hardware, disallowing the thief access to the protected data. This has changed over time with the introduction of optional data authentication/integrity verification.<ref>{{cite web
| url=https://docs.freebsd.org/cgi/getmsg.cgi?fetch=326862+0+archive/2006/freebsd-current/20060611.freebsd-current
| title=Data authentication for geli(8) committed to HEAD.
| first=Pawel Jakub
| last=Dawidek
| date=2006-06-08
| access-date=2015-06-14}}</ref>

geli allows the key to consist of several information components (a user entered passphrase, random bits from a file, etc.), permits up to 2 keys (a user key and a company key, for example),<ref name="g_eli.h:255">{{cite web |title=g_eli.h:255 |url=https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/releng/14.0/sys/geom/eli/g_eli.h#L255 |access-date=5 January 2024}}</ref> and can attach a provider with a random, one-time key. The user passphrase is strengthened with [[PKCS#5]].<ref name="manpage">{{cite web
| url=https://www.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?query=geli
| title=GELI(8)
| work=FreeBSD man pages
| access-date=2015-06-14}}</ref>

== Differences from GBDE ==
The geli utility is different from [[gbde]] in that it offers different features and uses a different scheme for doing cryptographic work. It supports the crypto framework within FreeBSD, allowing hardware cryptographic acceleration if available, as well as supporting more cryptographic algorithms (currently [[Advanced Encryption Standard|AES]], [[Triple DES]], [[Blowfish (cipher)|Blowfish]] and [[Camellia (cipher)|Camellia]]) and data authentication/integrity verification via [[MD5]], [[SHA1]], [[RIPEMD160]], [[SHA256]], [[SHA384]] or [[SHA512]] as [[HMAC|Hash Message Authentication Code]]s.<ref name="manpage"/>
